evidence_set: A single-author review searching 1990 to 2004, with earlier studies also included for symptoms the 1990 review had left unclear: more than 3,500 citations, 792 abstracts read, 290 articles read and 120 cited; inclusion required published prospective studies of cigarettes with more than 18 hours of abstinence; the author chose which results to include on his subjective opinion of rigor, consistency and size, and states that data collection and interpretation rested solely on his judgments.

Difficulty concentrating peaked in the first few days and lasted from a week or less to 4 weeks or more; impatience rose for 3 to 4 weeks or more in all 3 newer studies; sleep fragmentation (waking at night) increased consistently in sleep-EEG and clinical studies lasting 5 to 14 days, with more recall of vivid dreams; restlessness peaked on days 1 to 3 and lasted 2 to 4 weeks (1 week in one study).

evidence_set: Every study favoured exercise, from −0.22 to −4.54 points for strength of desire; the three studies that included isometric exercise had among the smallest effects, with intervals including zero in two of them for strength of desire (−0.55 and −0.22), and the largest effect came from the study with the highest baseline craving.

Titles were screened by the first author alone; quality was reported only as randomization (one study allocated by recruitment order); the review was paid for from internal institutional funds, and the authors report no connection with the tobacco or pharmaceutical industries; editors' count from the reference list and the text: 17 of the 19 included trials list at least one of the review's authors.

evidence_set: Craving was absent in the late crash and during heavy sleep; over 80% used sedatives (including alcohol or opiates) at least once to sleep; five people whose ordered cocaine arrived 2 to 5 hours after their last dose did not use it; eight people described a crash of at most 3 days and the rest up to 6 days, while the figure gives 9 hours to 4 days.

All people with other diagnoses and four others were treated with medication, so the later phases were not observed without it in most; the authors call the findings preliminary, limited by small numbers and the lack of structured instruments or blind observation in parts of the study; editors' count: 20 of the 30 took medication.

In a controlled residential study, all the men with cocaine dependence reported last using cocaine within 48 hours before admission; mood distress and craving were highest on admission day and fell over the 28 days (craving F = 17.270, P<.01); sleep reports did not differ from controls except more difficulty falling asleep and a greater improvement in clear-headedness on arising.

evidence_set: Sleep reports did not differ from controls except more difficulty falling asleep in the cocaine group throughout (group F = 10.428) and a greater improvement in clear-headedness on arising in the cocaine group (interaction F = 2.001); the other sleep measures improved over time in both groups; weight gain of 4.6 kg against 3.8 kg did not differ; heart rate rose 10.9 beats a minute in the cocaine group and fell 2.3 in controls.
